Yes—most likely.

At **3.75° altitude**, the Moon’s center is above the astronomical horizon, roughly **four finger-widths above a perfectly level east-southeastern horizon** at azimuth **113°**. A **43% illuminated Moon** is bright and ordinarily easy to see with unaided vision in a clear, dark sky.

The main uncertainty is the **local horizon**. At such a low altitude:

- buildings, trees, hills, or the Denver-area terrain may block it;
- atmospheric haze and extinction will dim and redden it;
- refraction and app/terrain inaccuracies can shift the apparent situation somewhat.

So if you have an unobstructed view toward **east-southeast**, you would probably spot it. From a typical location with nearby obstructions, it could easily be hidden. It would also be **descending and close to setting**, not rising.
